articles.title: Sara Duterte: So, who’s behind attacks against me? It’s Marcos.
articles.summary: 'Sino ang nasa likod ng paninira sa akin? Administrasyon. Ang Palasyo, si BBM,' Duterte says as she denies Gracioso’s allegations of multimillion-peso deliveries

blocks.text: 'Sino ang nasa likod ng paninira sa akin? Administrasyon. Ang Palasyo, si BBM,' Duterte says as she denies Gracioso’s allegations of multimillion-peso deliveries

items: Vice President Sara Duterte is facing allegations of corruption linked to former cop Rodulfo Gracioso Jr., which she attributes to a smear campaign orchestrated by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his administration.
Duterte denies the allegations, claiming Gracioso is lying and motivated by personal grievances, while the Palace asserts that she is responsible for her own predicament due to her actions.

Duterte is currently undergoing an impeachment trial, and if convicted, she could be removed from office and barred from future political positions, raising questions about her continued blame on Marcos for her misfortunes.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
Vice President Sara Duterte, the country’s second-highest official, has a pattern of linking her misfortunes to former ally President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.
Now that she is facing allegations involving millions of pesos in deliveries by former cop Rodulfo Gracioso Jr., Duterte points to no one but her 2022 presidential candidate.

“Sino ang nasa likod ng paninira sa akin? Administrasyon. Ang Palasyo, si BBM (Bongbong Marcos). Makikita ‘nyo naman ‘yong mga declarations, mga statements ng Office of the President eh. ‘Di ba? Andiyan pa ‘yong impeachment nila,” Duterte said during a press conference in Davao City on Tuesday, October 6.

(Who’s behind the smear campaign against me? The administration. The Palace, BBM. You will see in the declarations, statements of the Office of the President, right? They still have their impeachment.)

Gracioso, in his eight-page affidavit submitted to the National Bureau of Investigation, claimed that he delivered millions of pesos to the Vice President when she was Davao City mayor. This happened more than 10 times, alleged the dismissed cop.
He also claimed that the money came from Duterte ally, former House speaker Lord Allan Velasco, while former Davao City information officer Jefry Tupas allegedly received it on Duterte’s behalf.

“Kung makikita ‘nyo, ang ginagawa ng communications ng administrasyon, lahat no’ng bahid na katiwalian na dapat sagutin ni BBM ay pinapahid niya sa akin. So ang ginawa nila, ‘Oh, para ano, sabihin na siya din, gawa tayo ng [issue].’ Ang hindi nila alam, nagsisinungaling si Gracioso kaya nga nakikita ‘yong mga kasinungalingan doon sa archives,” Duterte added.

(As you can see, the administration’s communications team is throwing all the corruption allegations facing BBM at me. They thought, “Let’s drag her into it, let’s make an issue out of it.” What they do not know is that Gracioso is lying, as shown by the archives.)
Duterte devoted more than an hour of her press conference to denying Gracioso’s allegations. She said the former cop was motivated by his anger toward the Velascos and by money.

blocks.caption: Sara Duterte denies Gracioso’s claims, says he’s motivated by money

blocks.text: But for Malacañang, Duterte is responsible for her own predicament. Palace press officer Undersecretary Claire Castro said the allegations facing the Vice President stemmed from her own actions.

“Kung may sumisira man kay Bise Presidente, siya ang may kagagawan no’n sa sarili niya. Sila ang nakinabang sa bawat sentimo na nakukuha nila o nadedeposito sa kanilang accounts ng mga banyaga at ‘di umanong drug lords,” Castro told Rappler in a message.
“Ang sarap at pagpapasasa ay nasa kanila kaya, huwag magturo sa iba kapag nagkakabulgaran na ng mga anomalya. Panindigan nila ang mga ginawa nila,” she added.

(If there is anything damaging the Vice President, it is her own actions. They are the ones who benefited from every centavo they received or deposited into their accounts from foreign entities and alleged drug lords. They benefited from it, so they should not blame others when they are exposed. They should stand by their actions.)
Again, it was no surprise that Duterte dragged Marcos’ name into the Gracioso allegations.

Just last month, on September 7, Duterte said in a video statement that the sufferings of many Filipinos, including the widespread floodings, hunger, and high commodity prices, were caused by no less than the administration she backed in 2022.

Duterte is facing a grave threats case before Quezon City Regional Trial Court due to her alleged assassination threat against Marcos and his family. She posted bail on September 5 and claimed she did not feel safe in the country.

Then two days later, on September 7, she accused the Marcos government of “child abuse” because law enforcers allegedly subjected even her children to continued “surveillance.” Duterte’s own father, former president Rodrigo Duterte, is facing trial at the International Criminal Court due to his drug war that killed thousands of citizens, including women and children.

blocks.caption: The meltdown of Sara Duterte: From ‘no joke, no joke’ to ‘I do not feel safe’

blocks.text: Duterte is now in the middle of her impeachment trial. If convicted, she will be removed as vice president and barred from holding public office – and from seeking the presidential seat in 2028.
And if this comes to pass, will Marcos once again be named as the convenient culprit – her erstwhile ally and old friend who somehow remains responsible for her every new misfortune? – Rappler.com

articles.title: Salubong sa Sandaan: Miriam College marks 100 years with day-to-midnight festivities
articles.summary: The institution's centennial celebrations bridged generations, honoring its trailblazers and inspiring the bright potential of its students.

blocks.text: The institution's centennial celebrations bridged generations, honoring its trailblazers and inspiring the bright potential of its students.

items: Miriam College celebrated its centennial year with a festive event called Salubong sa Sandaan, which included a Marian procession, a Centennial Mass, and a film festival showcasing student and employee works.
The celebration continued with a Centennial Night at Fairmont Hotel, featuring alumni gatherings, a fashion show, and the launch of a coffee table book documenting the institution's 100-year legacy.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

Editor’s note: This press release is sponsored by Miriam College and was handled by BrandRap, the sales and marketing arm of Rappler. No member of the news and editorial team participated in the publishing of this piece.

Miriam College (MC) ushered in its historic centennial year with Salubong sa Sandaan, a festive day-to-midnight event held on September 11 and extending into the early hours of September 12. The school community—comprising employees, students, and alumni—gathered at the Loyola Heights campus to mark this significant milestone and celebrate an institution whose century-long legacy is rooted in faith, education, service, and leadership.

blocks.caption: A TRADITION. The Cultural Classical Dance Club of Miriam College High School led the traditional Karakol to open the Marian Procession, leading to the Centennial Mass.

blocks.text: The celebration opened with the entire community praying the Holy Rosary in honor of Mother Mary, after whom the school was named. Miriam is the Aramaic name of Mother Mary. This was followed by the Karakol, a traditional Marian procession, and the celebration of the Centennial Mass officiated by Bishop Honesto Ontioco, D.D., of the Diocese of Cubao.

blocks.caption: ROOTED IN FAITH. Maryknoll Sisters in the Philippines and Miriam College’s past presidents Dr. Loreta N. Castro, Dr. Patricia B. Licuanan, and Amb. Laura Q. Del Rosario join the community during the celebratory mass.

blocks.text: The festivities continued throughout the evening with the screening of short films created by students and MC employees for the Miriam College Film Festival (MCFF). The program also featured the school’s homegrown talents from its three campuses—MC Loyola Heights, MC Nuvali, and MC Alviera.

blocks.caption: TO THE BEAT. Sole2Soul and Company of One, two of the College’s homegrown dance groups, brought rhythm and energy to the festivities.

blocks.text: A much-anticipated moment was the MCFF awarding ceremony led by Miriam College President Dr. Maria Regina Lizares and Human Resources Director Dr. Noel Racho.

blocks.caption: FIRST FILM FESTIVAL. The first Miriam College Film Festival (MCFF) themed Mga Kwento ng Isang Daan,features six original student and employee films inspired by the institution’s 100-year legacy.

blocks.text: The centennial celebration continued on September 12 as generations of Maryknoll and Miriam College alumni gathered at the Fairmont Hotel in Makati for the Centennial Night and the launch of the coffee table book, ‘The Legacy We Carry: 100 Years From Maryknoll to Miriam.’

blocks.caption: REUNITED. Maryknoll and Miriam College alumni honor fellow alumna and newly-conferred National Artist for Design, Maria Beatriz “Patis” Pamintuan Tesoro (center), during the Centennial Night celebrations at Fairmont Hotel in Makati.

HONORING THEIR ROOTS. Miriam College President Dr. Gina Lizares and Sr. Marvelous Misolas, M.M. (2nd and 3rd from right) join the Maryknoll-Miriam alumni at the Fairmont Hotel for the launch of the centennial book, ‘The Legacy We Carry: 100 Years from Maryknoll to Miriam.‘
BLUE AND GOLD. Miriam College’s official colors flooded the night from the vibrant hosts to the dynamic crowd.

blocks.text: The evening brought together alumni from across generations for a night of bonding, dancing, and music. A highlight of the celebration was a fashion show honoring alumni and newly conferred National Artist for Design Maria Beatriz “Patis” Pamintuan Tesoro.

blocks.caption: MC NUVALI REPRESENT! The campus’s Indayaw and Sikhayaw group wowed the community with their energetic moves.

blocks.text: From Maryknoll to Miriam, the institution’s influence on Philippine education—particularly women’s education—has become an enduring part of the nation’s history. From its beginnings in 1926 as a teacher-training school in Malabon–where it produced its first women graduates–the institution has gone on to nurture generations of students and distinguished alumni whose leadership and service have made a lasting impact across diverse fields, both in the Philippines and abroad. Today, Miriam College continues to expand its mission in education beyond the walls of its Loyola Heights campus with the opening of Miriam College Nuvali in 2014 and Miriam College Alviera in 2025.

blocks.caption: OVERFLOWING TALENT. Miriam College’s centennial celebration was held in the campus’ outdoor field from the morning of September 11 until midnight of September 12 to welcome another exciting century for the institution.
RYTHM AND ENERGY. Faculty and students in the crowd cheered for their favorite group performances throughout the night.

blocks.text: Miriam College’s year-long centennial celebration is expected to continue until September 2027, with a lineup of activities that will bring together the school community and its stakeholders. Among these are the Christmas Bazaar, a concert by the Miriam College Music Center, the MC100 Fun Run, and the Academic Conference on Teaching and Learning.

articles.title: Woman’s body found in stockyard trough close to NSW-Queensland border
articles.summary:
Police say body found by trail bike riders at remote farm in Terragon is badly decomposed, sparking search of missing persons records

  • Get our

blocks.text: A partially submerged body believed to be a woman has been discovered in a remote stockyard, with the death being treated as suspicious.
Officers were called to a property in Terragon, near Murwillumbah in northern NSW, at about 11.20am on Monday after reports of a dead body.
The body, which is yet to be identified, was found partially submerged in a disused stock dip, a large trough commonly used to bathe livestock in anti-parasite solutions, police said.
Police said the body was badly decomposed.
“The body is believed to be of a female, but due to the state of decomposition of that body I’m unable to provide further details,” Det Insp Matthew Zimmer told reporters in Tweed Heads on Tuesday.
“Due to the location of the body, the remoteness of the area, the absence of a vehicle or any other mode of transport, we are treating this death as suspicious.”
He said it was difficult to determine how long the remains had been at the site.
The grim discovery was made by two trail bike riders in an area deemed crown land.
A crime scene was set up overnight, with specialist forensic examiners combing the area.
Police were checking through missing persons registers in NSW and Queensland, Zimmer said.
after newsletter promotion
A postmortem examination is expected to be carried out in coming days to help identify the body and the cause of death.
Terragon is located in Tweed Shire, roughly 40km from the NSW-Queensland border.

articles.title: St. FX banner shows more work needed on sexual violence prevention, advocate says
articles.summary: A researcher on sexual violence says it's good that people are talking about the inappropriate banner displayed on an off-campus house during St. Francis Xavier University's homecoming, but the…

blocks.text: Nova Scotia

A researcher on sexual violence says it's good that people are talking about the inappropriate banner displayed on an off-campus house during St. Francis Xavier University's homecoming, but the conversation must continue.
Sign decried by university president who says a code of conduct investigation is underway
Off-campus sign depicting rape culture draws condemnation

A researcher into sexual violence prevention on university campuses says she sees a connection between the outcry over a banner that appeared during homecoming weekend at St. Francis Xavier University in Antigonish, N.S., and an alleged gang rape at Cornell University.

Alyssa Spridgeon says the public outcry over the St. FX banner has been fuelled in part by the recent outrage over how American authorities have handled the Cornell case in upstate New York. They initially decided not to lay charges, and that is now the subject of an inquiry ordered by New York’s governor.

Spridgeon says it’s a good thing people are focusing on this issue, but she said she hopes that interest in stopping sexual violence is sustained long after the Cornell case, or even the banner, disappears from the news.
“I would love to see people continue to advocate long-term, and not just when this story gets resolved or when it goes away,” Spridgeon said.
She hopes the conversation happening now helps people “understand how things like a sign or rape jokes or victim-blaming statements ... can contribute to a culture that perpetuates harm.”
St. FX professor Tara Taylor was driving home when she saw the sign hanging from an off-campus student rental house.
"I thought I should really take a photo of it to document this," she told CBC News. "This is not OK and I don't want to contribute to the silence around it."
Taylor said there was another sign at the home that was more offensive, but she chose not to take a photo of it.
She posted the photo to Facebook to see if others had the same visceral reaction as she did. Taylor said people generally did.
"I saw it as a taunt and just very much treating girlfriends as objects, as possessions," she said. "I just found it very offensive and part of rape culture. I didn't see it as just a joke."
Football player convicted for sex assaults

Spridgeon was an undergraduate student at St. FX when a member of the university football team was convicted for sexually assaulting two female students. Omogbolahan “Teddy” Jegede has since been released on day parole, having served his prison sentence. The two women have each launched civil lawsuits against the university.
The president of St. FX, Andrew Hakin, said a lot has changed since those assaults.
“We have gone through our policies very carefully,” he said Monday, adding the school has adjusted its policies as well.
Hakin said he couldn’t comment further on the Jegede case or the subsequent lawsuits, but he expressed frustration and disappointment about the banner that appeared on the weekend.
“We don't want behaviours that objectify women in this way, that normalizes sexual violence and is indicative of a rape culture,” Hakin said.
“This is not who we are.”
Spridgeon said she has seen a wide range of reactions to the banner after a photo was posted online, from rationalizing them with a “boys will be boys” attitude all the way to expressions of outrage.
Hakin said a student code of conduct investigation is already underway and he expects to see results within two weeks. He said sanctions could include suspension or expulsion.
During her time at St. FX, Spridgeon worked with varsity athletes, talking to them about sexual violence. She was a varsity athlete herself, playing goal for the university soccer team.

She’s now part of a research project looking at sexual violence in university sports across the Maritimes. The team is reaching out to present and former athletes to try to persuade them to talk about their experiences.
She said the banners displayed this weekend show there’s still more work to do.
“I'd love to see people taking steps to interrupt conversations in their daily life, calling out or calling people in to conversation to discuss why what they're saying isn't appropriate," she said.
Spridgeon says those interventions are a preventative approach to prevent more harmful behaviours in the long term.
"When we're excusing the banners or excusing harmful jokes, we're sending the message that we're going to excuse other things as well, like sexual assault.”

articles.title: France: Trade unions join students in major demonstration
articles.summary: Tens of thousands are expected at nationwide protests against poor learning conditions for students in France.

image.caption: Rights groups have accused the police of using disproportionate force on children.Image: Raphael Lafargue/abaca/picture alliance

blocks.text: A day of nationwide blockades and street protests are planned on Tuesday in France, led by high-school and trade union groups. Tens of thousands are expected to take to the streets.
The demonstrations are part of a movement that sprung in recent weeks demanding that french President Emmanuel Macron's government tackle understaffed and underfunded schools.
Protests that began in Paris's deprived suburbs have now spread across the country, including pupils from affluent areas who have joined in solidarity.

Hundreds of high school entrances have been blocked by student protesters since late September. The students have decried poor learning conditions, such as missing teachers, overloaded timetables, dilapidated classrooms and buildings that are not suitable for high temperatures.

While many of the demonstrations have been peaceful, some protesters have lit trash can fires, destroyed bus shelters or clashed with riot police, who have responded with batons, tear gas and riot-control rounds, with authorities accusing the movement of having devolved into urban violence.

blocks.caption: Rights groups have accused the police of using disproportionate force on children.Image: Raphael Lafargue/abaca/picture alliance

blocks.text: Police accused of brutality towards children
The country's Justice Ministry said that 5,060 people have been arrested since the protests began. Some 87% of those taken into custody were minors.
Over 1,800 people face charges, including 1,483 minors, the ministry said, without ​providing details of what they had been accused of, although some 790 cases have alaready been dismissed.

Trade unions and human rights groups have accused the police of using disproportionate force on children. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said on Monday that police have launched 10 internal investigations into allegations of brutality since the protests started.

Among the reports, a 15-year-old lost his hand at a protest in the northern town of Lens, a 16-year-old lost the use of his right eye after being seriously injured in the head in the central town of Tours, while in Saint-Ouen-L'Aumone, northwest of Paris, a 14-year-old lost most of his teeth when a police officer appeared to fire a projectile at him at very close range.

blocks.caption: Students have demanded that the governmetn improve learning conditionsImage: Raphael Lafargue/abaca/picture alliance

blocks.text: Government promises response
French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said he had ‌ordered government ministers to study the students' leading demands.
Among the demands the government will be tackling are ensuring absent teachers are replaced, reviewing the ‌length ​of the 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. school day and the need for longer lunch breaks.
The government has promised to also look at repairs needed to ageing school buildings.
Lecornu said ministers are expected to submit their first proposals by the end of October. The ​protests have put pressure on a government that has sought to narrow a ballooning budget deficit.

articles.title: Kenya confirms its first Ebola death as outbreak spreads
articles.summary: The patient has been living in DR Congo for the past seven years.

blocks.text: Kenya has confirmed its first case of Ebola - a Kenyan citizen who has been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo for the past seven years.
Health Minister Aden Duale said the patient, who fell ill a month ago, and was treated in several hospitals in DR Congo, died days after arriving in Nairobi.

Duale said the patient boarded a flight on Saturday and underwent normal public screening at the main airport in Nairobi before he was transferred by a relative to a hospital in the city. Tests conducted confirmed positive for Ebola Bundibugyo virus.
More than 4,000 people have died from Ebola in DR Congo this year, in what is the second most deadly known outbreak of the disease.

The outbreak spread to Uganda, which reported 20 cases and two ⁠deaths, but the World Health Organization declared Uganda ​free ​of the disease in ​August.

articles.title: Sara Duterte says her father Rodrigo still remembers her
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte on Tuesday disputed claims that her father, former President Rodrigo Duterte, who is detained in The Hague, Netherlands, over crimes against humanity charges, had…

blocks.text: Published October 6, 2026 4:44pm

Vice President Sara Duterte on Tuesday disputed claims that her father, former President Rodrigo Duterte, who is detained in The Hague, Netherlands, over crimes against humanity charges, had forgotten her.
Speaking at a press conference in Davao City, Duterte said her father recently called her, dismissing claims that the 81-year old former president could no longer remember his children.
“Yes, forgetful si PRRD, pero tumawag siya sa akin nung… bago lang. So hindi niya ako nakalimutan. Sinabihan ko siya, bakit ngayon ka lang tumawag sa akin. Ang tagal mo nang hindi tumawag,” she said.
(Yes, PRRD is forgetful, but he called me just recently. So he has not forgotten me. I told him, why are you only calling me now? It’s been so long since you last called me.)
Over the weekend, former presidential spokesperson Harry Roque claimed that Duterte could no longer determine the passage of time or recall the names of his children and grandchildren.
The claim comes as Duterte’s defense team continues to challenge his fitness to stand trial before the International Criminal Court (ICC), citing alleged cognitive and memory problems.
The ICC has ordered an updated assessment of Duterte’s fitness for the trial phase, after an earlier assessment found him fit to participate in pretrial proceedings.
According to the vice president, her father told her during their call, “Wala lang. Nangamusta lang ako sa imoha.”
(He said, ‘Nothing. I just wanted to check on you’.)
“Sabi niya ikaw kasi ang tumawag sa akin,” she said.
(He said, “You should be the one to call me.”)
Duterte said she explained to her father that she could not call him directly and that he had to ask the authorities at his detention facility to connect him to her.
“Sabi ko, hindi nga kasi pwede. Dapat ikaw ang magsabi doon sa—diyan sa loob na tawagan mo ako. Kasi hindi man kami maka-dial, makatawag doon papasok. Pwede lang palabas siya tumawag,” she added.
(I said, “No, because it’s not possible. You have to tell those inside there to call me. Because we can’t dial or make calls to them. He can only make outgoing calls.”)
Duterte said she did not tell her father about what was happening to her.

“Actually, wala namang nangyayari sa akin. Political lang naman lahat ang nangyayari. Sinabi ko lang sa kanya na bibisita ako sa ganito na dates, okay lang ba sa’yo. Sabi niya sige, okay na ’yan,” she said.
(Actually, nothing is happening to me. Everything that is happening is just political. I just told him that I would visit on these dates, is that okay with you? He said, “Sure, that’s okay.”)

Duterte is facing an impeachment trial over allegations that she made grave threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and others, misused confidential funds, had unexplained wealth and engaged in bribery.
She is also facing three counts of grave threats before a Quezon City court.

In September, dismissed policeman Rodulfo Gracioso Jr. claimed that he delivered cash to Sara Duterte, Davao City 1st District Rep. Paolo Duterte and the former President Rodrigo Duterte, allegedly on the instructions of former House Speaker Lord Allan Velasco.

Meanwhile, Rodrigo Duterte is facing crimes against humanity charges before the ICC in connection with killings linked to his war on drugs when he was mayor of Davao City and later when he was president.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Fact check: Viral fire trikes falsely tagged at P10 million each
articles.summary: Viral posts falsely tagged fire trikes at P10 million each, linking them to a separate planned fire truck deal.

blocks.text: The Local Government Unit of Naval, Biliran, held the blessing of three brand-new three-wheeled fire suppression penetrators and a backhoe loader on July 10, 2026.
LGU Naval / Facebook
MANILA, Philippines — Multiple social media posts falsely claim that fire trikes shown in different localities cost P10 million each.

In an October 4 reel, a Facebook user showed a row of fire trikes in a municipality alongside a clip of Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla saying that the fire trucks the government plans to procure would cost P10 million each, down from the previous P16-million price tag.
Facebook posts falsely claimed that fire trikes shown in San Antonio, Nueva Ecija, and Naval, Biliran, cost P10 million each.
Screenshot taken Oct. 6, 2026, 4 p.m.
The post’s caption read:
Mga Ma'am sir sound check tayo sa bagong fire truck ???? ng BBM admin????

Another Facebook post on October 5 compared a photo of the fire trikes with fire trucks in Japan, criticizing the administration of President Bongbong Marcos and also claiming that each fire trike costs P10 million.

nagyabang si Baby M na magpapalipad daw ng rocket... eh fire truck nga di makabili..rocket pa kaya..imbis na mag modernize ng fire truck...ginawang fire trike.. paurong ang pag usad.. pabalik sa sina unang panahon.. salamat kay jonvic... 10M each daw.. alams na kung bakit?? kasi wala na pera ang goberno.. inubos na nila..
Rating: This is false.
Facts
Remulla’s recent statement about the planned procurement of fire trucks at P10 million each is being falsely linked to fire trikes obtained months ago in separate localities.
In an October 3 statement, Remulla said they will be traveling to South Korea in two weeks to sign a government-to-government agreement to purchase 1,500 fire trucks.
According to the Interior Secretary, the BFP previously purchased fire trucks at around P16 million each. Under the planned agreement, the fire trucks would cost P10 million per unit.
“In two weeks, when we sign our agreement, the fire trucks will only be P10 million each, a savings of P9 billion over three years,” he said.
The deal has yet to be finalized, while the fire trikes shown in the circulating photos and videos were already unveiled in July 2026.
A Facebook post showed six three-wheeled Fire Fighter Rescue Vehicles unveiled by the Local Government Unit of San Antonio, Nueva Ecija, on July 6, 2026.

The video stitched alongside Remulla in the viral Facebook reel was taken in San Antonio, Nueva Ecija, on July 6, where Mayor Gege Salonga-Esquivel unveiled six new three-wheeled Fire Fighter Rescue Vehicles purchased by the local government.

"Ang mga sasakyang ito ay magsisilbing dagdag na lakas sa ating emergency response at ilalaan sa mga malalayong barangay upang mas mabilis na maabot ang ating mga kababayan sa oras ng pangangailangan," Salonga-Esquievel said.
A Facebook post showed three fire suppression penetrators unveiled by the Local Government Unit of Naval, Biliran, on July 10, 2026.
Meanwhile, the Facebook post featuring a photo of fire trikes alongside fire trucks said to be in Japan was taken in Naval, Biliran, on July 10.

The local government unit (LGU) of Naval held the blessing of three brand-new fire suppression penetrators and a backhoe loader in celebration of Disaster Resilience Month. The fire suppression penetrators are also three-wheeled vehicles.

"The fire suppression penetrators, designed to maneuver through narrow streets and congested residential areas, will enable faster and more efficient fire suppression response in zones previously inaccessible to conventional fire trucks," LGU Naval said in a post.
Why we fact-checked this

The posts gained thousands of engagements and circulated amid the ongoing impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, with both accounts having previously posted content supportive of the Dutertes and critical of Marcos, including the claims featuring the fire trikes.
As of October 6, the Facebook reel has garnered over 7,000 likes, 1,500 comments and 1,200 shares. Meanwhile, the Facebook post has obtained more than 1,200 reactions, 200 comments, and 100 shares.

MANILA, Philippines — A total of 106 cities and municipalities across the country have been officially declared under a state of calamity as the effects of the ongoing El Niño phenomenon continue to intensify, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC) said.
In its latest report on Tuesday, October 6, the NDRRMC said the dry spell has affected 104,149 families, or 388,375 people.
The following are the numbers of areas under a state of calamity per region:

items: Region 2: 66 cities/municipalities
CARAGA: 23 cities/municipalities
Region 5: 12 cities/municipalities
CALABARZON: Four cities/municipalities
Region 12: One city/municipality

blocks.text: Out of the 35,893 families identified as requiring urgent assistance, the government has successfully assisted 24,618 families.
The total cost of assistance provided so far stands at P39,058,681.06, distributed as follows:

items: CARAGA: P23,091,638 provided to 11,672 families
Region 2: P9,927,750 provided to 1,891 families
Region 5: P6,039,293.06 provided to 11,055 families

blocks.text: The agricultural sector has also suffered losses.
Citing data from the Department of Agriculture, a total of P5,580,172,296.84 in damages was recorded.

Region 2 recorded the highest agricultural damage, accounting for over P4.96 billion of the total losses.

In the CARAGA region, 39 wild, forest, and mountain fire incidents have been reported. CARAGA has also experienced water supply interruptions across four cities and municipalities, though supplies have since been restored.

“It’s really scary not knowing what you’re going to do … what the future holds, I guess. Nothing is guaranteed.”
The young woman spoke with CBC News on the condition of anonymity given the sensitive nature of her experience as a youth in care.

Aside from a pre-arranged meeting with income support two months before her birthday, she said there was no plan to prepare her for aging out of care — when her voluntary youth services agreement with the province was set to expire.
“I didn't feel prepared whatsoever. I was having a really hard time, even mentally it was taking a toll on me. I wasn’t ready for it,” she said.
In Newfoundland and Labrador, youth who are in need of protective care between the ages of 16 and 17 can sign on with the province for an individualized youth services plan.
In this province, youth lose access to their financial and social support on their 21st birthday. It’s one of the youngest age limits in the country.
However, the province says there are exceptions.
Adjusting out of system can be challenging
“I think it’s leaving a lot of young people behind,” said Shelby Arnold, educational program lead with Thrive, a non-profit organization in St. John’s.
Heavy workloads on social workers limit one-on-one time with youth and the adjustment from group care — where daily choices can be dictated — to sudden autonomy can be jarring, Arnold said.
“Often [social workers are] seeing people once a month,” Arnold said.
“Social workers don't have the capacity, even though they would be in the right position to do that work.”
Organizations like Thrive try to fill that gap, Arnold said, but non-profits are not a catch-all.
Madison Pretty examined the province’s youth services program while completing her master's degree in public policy at Simon Fraser University.
Pretty spoke with youth who left the system, social workers and non-profit organizations that work with young people first hand.
“What we found was that what's in the policy manual, what's in the legislation, is not what's happening in practice,” Pretty said in a recent interview.
“The young people that I spoke to really described not feeling like there was any really kind of transition.”

Financial and social supports vary for youth who are in the child protection system depending on the province. In Nova Scotia, for example, the government recently raised the age limit to 26. However, critics argue even that doesn’t go far enough.
“Newfoundland and Labrador is lagging quite behind,” Pretty said. “We're tied with one other province for having the youngest cutoff age.”
Pretty recommends the province extend the age mandate to give youth time to build skills without dreading a "looming birthday care cliff."
She added it’s also one of the only provinces without mandatory transition planning, to prepare youth for independent adulthood.
Daniel Hepditch, an education outreach worker at Thrive, said things need to improve.
“If not raise the age, adjust the transition process and the phasing,” Hepditch said.
“I think that our province needs to do something to make this better for our young people.”

However, Hepditch and Arnold caution about the use of mandatory transition planning, empathizing with the importance of social workers being prepared to adapt to changes and approaching youth at their own pace.
Abrupt independence: Newfoundland and Labrador has one of the lowest cutoff ages in Canada for youth leaving system
The consequences of poor planning and preparation can be stark, according to a report released by a Senate committee in December.
The report offered a stinging assessment of the country’s child protection systems and the lack of support for youth transitioning into adulthood.
Independent Senator Mary Coyle told CBC News last winter that far too often the system acts as a “child welfare to prison pipeline.”
“When young people age out of care, where do they go? How do they feed themselves? How do they house themselves? Who do they associate with?” Coyle said.
“If there isn't a wrap-around healthy support system for that person, they're going to seek out a system somewhere to get by.”
At Thrive, Arnold and Hepditch work with youth to improve their education. They see the success stories, in spite of the challenges handed to young people.
“We see the capacity and we see all the wonderful gifts and strengths that people and care have,” Arnold said.
“And so, they're not a problem to fix. They're people who are trying to step into the next phase of their life and we all can do a little bit better to make sure that they have what they need.”
Minister of Social Supports and Well-being Chris Tibbs was not made available for an interview.

EDITOR'S NOTE: They are among society's most vulnerable: children who experience traumatic instability and end up in government care. In this series called “Left Behind,” the CBC Atlantic investigative team explores the challenges and outcomes through the eyes of people who lived through this and those trying to help them.

Ariana Kelland is a reporter with the CBC Newfoundland and Labrador bureau in St. John's. She is working as a member of CBC's Atlantic Investigative Unit. Email: ariana.kelland@cbc.ca

articles.title: Negros Trade Fair 2026 doubles last year’s attendance at SMX Aura
articles.summary: SM and ANP welcomed nearly 80,000 visitors to BÚTLAK, setting a new benchmark for the Negros Trade Fair in Manila.

items: The 40th Negros Trade Fair attracted nearly 80,000 visitors, doubling last year's attendance.
The event generated nearly P118 million in sales, with P75 million from spot sales, indicating strong consumer demand, particularly in the food section where many exhibitors sold out early.
The fair highlighted a blend of heritage and innovation, with established brands and younger entrepreneurs presenting fresh takes on traditional products.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

Editor’s note: This press release is sponsored by SM Supermalls and was handled by BrandRap, the sales and marketing arm of Rappler. No member of the news and editorial team participated in the publishing of this piece.

BÚTLAK: The 40th Negros Trade Fair welcomed 79,512 visitors to SMX Convention Center Aura from September 22 to 27—double last year’s attendance and the highest foot traffic recorded in the fair’s Manila run. Organized by the Association of Negros Producers (ANP), in partnership with SM Supermalls through SM for MSMEs, and the Provincial Government of Negros Occidental, the six-day fair brought together 126 exhibitors across 177 booths. Visitors came to explore the food, fashion, crafts, home finds, and travel stories of the Negros Island Region—and left with more than a few bags in hand.

blocks.caption: A TASTE OF NEGROS. From pantry staples and artisanal preserves to freshly made delicacies, visitors filled their bags with food finds that carried the flavors and stories of Negros beyond the fair.

blocks.text: BÚTLAK generated nearly P118 million in reported sales, based on submissions from 120 exhibitors, with six reports still being consolidated. Of this amount, P75 million came from spot sales, a 39% increase year on year and a strong indicator of direct consumer demand. Another P43 million came from business-to-business transactions involving institutional buyers, retailers, distributors, and other partners.

blocks.caption: ONE BITE AT A TIME. From comforting bowls and smoky grilled favorites to sweet local treats, BÚTLAK gave visitors a delicious way to experience the region’s rich culinary heritage.

blocks.text: The strong sales were evident in the food section, where several exhibitors—including Cocina Javellana, Bacolod Chicken House, and Wawa Bing’s Kitchen—sold out as early as the second day. Many food booths had also run through their inventory by late afternoon.

Among the fair’s crowd favorites were Bacolod Chicken House’s inasal 21’s batchoy, Vaca Japonesa’s Wagyu Kansi and Wagyu Tapa N Rice; Wawa Bings Kitchen’s fresh lumpia; Cocina Javellana’s ube halaya; Felicia’s ensaymada and El Ideal’s freshly made hot piaya. Visitors also sought out Ading’s Gourmet Kitchen’s batuan fruit paste, blue crab paste, and smoked bangus; Ereñeta-Manaloto Chorizo de Bacolod; Nanette’s VCO, coco cider vinegar, and sinamak; and Filipino favorites from Imay’s Bar & Restaurant. The results point to a clear opportunity for future editions: helping exhibitors prepare more inventory and production capacity to meet growing demand.

BÚTLAK’s strongest stories came from the meeting of legacy and new energy. Heritage brands continued to draw loyal customers, while younger founders and next-generation family members gave familiar products a fresh look, new flavors, and a stronger connection with today’s shoppers.

Bob’s, one of Bacolod’s most established food names, reintroduced itself through a retro-inspired Bob’s Sari-Sari Store concept, with members of the third generation helping man the booth. El Ideal, the heritage bakery founded in 1920, remained a crowd-drawer for its hot piaya while also attracting curiosity for its Guapple Pie. “We have been around for about 100 years because we never sacrificed quality,” said Maritess Sanchez of El Ideal. “The Negros Trade Fair has helped us expand our reach here in Manila.” The fair also made room for a newer generation of makers.

Upcycled by The Little Vintage Shop gave donated clothing a second life through circular fashion, while LAKAT featured locally made footwear incorporating pineapple-based textiles and other Philippine natural materials. NVC Foundation’s Artisans of Hope showcased handmade mosaic pieces that support Bacolod-based artisans, while Alter Trade Philippines connected shoppers to fair-trade products that support Negros sugarcane producers and rural livelihoods.

blocks.caption: FOR MSMEs. ANP president Christina Gaston spotted at the Negros Trade Fair.

blocks.text: “For ANP, MSME development is about giving people the opportunity to discover what they can create, what they can become, and where their creativity can take them,” said ANP president Christina Gaston.“Over 40 years, we have seen small businesses grow into enterprises and local products reach markets once thought beyond their reach.”

blocks.caption: DISCOVERING THE DETAILS. Shoppers browsed handwoven textiles, handcrafted bags and contemporary apparel, connecting directly with the artistry and stories woven into every Negrense creation.

blocks.text: The celebration opened with Arima, the symbolic ringing of the bell that traditionally marks the start of the workday—and, for BÚTLAK, the festive opening of Negros in Manila. At the heart of the annual ritual is food: an invitation for guests to experience Negrense ingredients, heritage and hospitality at the table.

This year, Manila chefs brought contemporary flair to familiar flavors and ingredients sourced from participating exhibitors. Negrense chef Don Colmenares of destination restaurant Sauma served Kansi Croquetas with Negros beef, batuan mayo and langka purée, alongside an Atcharang Ukoy with dilis polvoron, sinamak mayo and malunggay pesto.

Chef Luis Locsin presented his signature Negrense-inspired pâté en croûte creations: a Pork and Native Chicken Mosaic Pâté en Croûte with native chicken, Victorias ham, dried fruits, almonds and Don Papa Rum; and a Pork and Duck Pâté en Croûte with Victorias bacon, oyster mushrooms, herbs and port wine. Chef Cara Davis of Halong created a Saravia Coconut Crab Lumpia, served with coconut chutney, atchara, fermented garlic, kiwot honey and Vietnamese green chili sauce.

Official caterer Epicura, the catering arm of Curio led by Pia Lago and chef Bettina Arguelles, completed the spread with KBL rillette on oat thins, seasonal seafood kinilaw with tultul salt, crab bibingka with calcag dust and bihod, corned beef kansi with kansi gravy, pancit luglug molo, and pork bellychon with batuan chimichurri.

New to this year’s Arima, private chef Bea Magalona reimagined familiar favorites through an Adobarquillo—barquillos filled with Ilonggo-style adobo cream—and Piaya Toast, made with langka piaya, kadyos hummus and pork. Together, the Arima menu showed how the flavors of Negros can remain rooted in heritage while finding fresh expression through a new generation of chefs and culinary collaborators.
For SM Supermalls, BÚTLAK demonstrates how access to the right marketplace can help local businesses reach more customers and create new opportunities for growth.

blocks.caption: SM Supermalls’ executive vice president for marketing Joaquin San Agustin.

blocks.text: “Every purchase does more than bring home a piece of Negros,” said Joaquin L. San Agustin, executive vice president for marketing at SM Supermalls, during the opening. “It supports a local business, celebrates Filipino creativity, and helps another entrepreneurial story move forward.”

blocks.caption: CREATIVE COMMUNITY VISITS. Familiar faces from fashion, food, design and entertainment joined shoppers at BÚTLAK, exploring the people, products and stories that made the 40th Negros Trade Fair a standout Manila gathering.

blocks.text: Through SM for MSMEs, SM Supermalls works with partners such as ANP to help open doors for homegrown businesses—connecting them to shoppers, visibility, and bigger opportunities to grow. With nearly 80,000 visitors and nearly ₱118 million in reported sales, BÚTLAK’s milestone edition showed that when local products are given room to be discovered, the impact reaches far beyond the fair itself. It creates new possibilities for the people, families, and communities behind every product. BÚTLAK: The 40th Negros Trade Fair was organized by the Association of Negros Producers in partnership with SM Supermalls and the Provincial Government of Negros Occidental. — Rappler.com

articles.title: Escudero: Sara Duterte, husband's total net worth doesn't match bank transactions
articles.summary: The total net worth of Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband, Manases Carpio, as stated in their joint Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN) from 2002 to 2025 does not match…

blocks.text: Published October 6, 2026 4:28pm

The total net worth of Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband, Manases Carpio, as stated in their joint Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN) from 2002 to 2025 does not match the millions of bank transactions under their name, Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero said Tuesday.

At the same time, Escudero said that the P4.4 billion of covered and suspicious bank transactions from 2007 to 2025 recorded under the couple's name do not match their joint SALN declarations covering the same period.
Escudero made the observation based on the testimony of Anti-Money Laundering Council Executive Director Ronel Buenaventura before the Senate impeachment court

“P424 million ang pumasok at lumabas sa bank accounts ni Vice President Duterte at ng kanyang asawa from 2022 to 2025. I try to bring things in its absurd possibility to find out and test the hypothesis. In-add ko iyong SALN ng Pangalawang Pangulo mula 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025. Hindi naman dapat i-add ‘yun kasi iba’t ibang taon. [Pero] in total, P336 million. Hindi pa rin umabot ng P424 million,” Escudero said during Day 34 of the impeachment trial of Duterte.
(P424 million inflows and outflows from 2025 to 2025. I added the SALN from 2022 to 2025. Actually, you cannot add it but even so, the total is P336 million. It won't reach P424 million.)
“Meaning to say, on the assumption na walang ginastos mula sa lahat na assets nila at lahat na dineposit sa bangko, hindi pa rin aabot sa ganiting kalaking halaga,” he added.
(Even if they left their entire assets untouched and just deposited them all in banks, it won't reach that amount.)

Escudero said the case is the same for the P4.4 billion worth of covered and suspicious bank transactions under the names of Vice President and her husband from 2007 to 2025 when compared with SALNs for the same period.

“Yung P4.4 billion covering the period 2007 to 2025. Again, I bring it to its absurd point. We tried to add to all of the amounts in the combined SALNs for those covered period of 2007 to 2025. It totaled only P840 million,” he said.
“You would need five times at least five times of the combined SALN [net worth] total from 2007 to 2025 to be able to explain the huge amount of P4.4 billion in [bank] transactions,” he added.
In both instances, Escudero asked Buenaventura what would be the possible arithmetic that would match the SALN declarations with bank transactions.
“Can you explain how it could reach that amount knowing that the highest SALN in 2025 was at P98 million and the lowest SALN in 2007 was at P7 million? Can you explain it, Sir,” he said.
Buenaventura replied, “I am unable to explain or answer that, Your Honor.”
Escudero pressed, “But in the realm of possibilities, is there a possible explanation that can come to your mind as to how this can be? If you know.”
The AMLC official responded by saying, “On top of my head, nahihirapan po ako. Apologies po. I cannot explain it (It is really tough to explain).” —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: NBI confirms Velasco couple owns 2 alleged ‘cash houses’ in Pasig
articles.summary: The NBI said Velasco spouses own 2 alleged “cash houses” in Pasig and are linked to 2 Marinduque resorts under investigation.

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Initial validations by the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) have confirmed that former House Speaker Lord Allan Velasco and his wife, Rowena, own two alleged "cash houses" in Pasig City, along with two beach resorts in Marinduque that are being probed for suspicious financial activities.

NBI Director Melvin Matibag said on Tuesday, October 6, that they have established the ownership following the claims of dismissed policeman Rodulfo Gracioso Jr. that Velasco and his wife bought properties to store large volumes of cash during the lawmaker’s term as House speaker.

“Basically, nitong mga nakaraang araw ang vinalidate natin ‘yung claim niya doon sa cash houses na sinasabi and we’re able to establish, dun sa seven cash houses na sinasabi, we’ve already established two that are owned by Velasco spouses,” Matibag said.

(Basically, these past few days, we validated his claims about cash houses, and we’re able to establish that among the alleged seven cash houses, we’ve already established two that are owned by Velasco spouses.)
Both houses were located in Valle Verde 2 in Pasig: one on Champaca Street, and another on Sampaguita Street, according to Matibag.
The NBI said investigators checked land titles and Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) records in validating the ownership.
'Cash houses'
In his affidavit, Gracioso claimed Velasco was the primary source and coordinator of multi-million-peso cash deliveries to Vice President Sara Duterte.
The cash, he claimed, came from the 25% “all-in” kickbacks on government projects across the country.

He said the cash was initially packed and stored at the residence of Velasco and his wife at No. 142 Sampaguita St., Valle Verde 2, but the money grew too large, which made the former lawmaker buy at least six additional houses where they could store the money.
Velasco and Duterte have earlier denied Gracioso’s claims.
The NBI said the established ownership of the two houses in Pasig by Velasco has so far supported Gracioso’s claims.

“Dun sa mga claims ni Mr. Gracioso ng bahay at pag-aari ng mga Velasco, tumatama na. Especially lalo na doon sa bahay because ‘yung bahay it was named under Eagle Assets and Realty na ang presidente nito si Ms. Rowena Velasco,” Matibag said.

(The claims of Mr. Gracioso on residences and properties are beginning to be validated. Especially on the houses, because the houses were named under Eagle Assets and Realty, whose president is Ms. Rowena Velasco.)
Resorts in Marinduque
Aside from the houses in Pasig, the NBI said it also looked into Gracioso’s claims that Velasco was investing a lot of money into two resorts at Poctoy White Beach in Torrijos, Marinduque.
Matibag said the Sara Resort and Cabanas and Amara Resort and Villas were both linked to the Velasco spouses.
“Napakalaking resort niyan. When we checked sa SEC ‘yung ownership, lumalabas na sa spouses Velasco. May mga inassign na na-share without consideration. So ini-investigate natin ‘yan,” Matibag said.
(That is a very big resort. When we checked the ownership on the SEC, it appears to belong to spouses Velasco. There were shares assigned without consideration. So we’re investigating that.)

NBI said the Sara Resort and Cabanas is operated by 888 Wealth Star Corp, where Rowena Velasco serves as president and chairman, holding 60% of the shares. The P20 million capital, the agency said, was reported to be fully paid in cash at incorporation.

The Amara Resorts and Villas, meanwhile, is operated by Amara Equity Ventures Inc., where Velasco and his wife were principal incorporators holding 80% of subscribed shares. The NBI said both transferred their original shareholdings to third parties in 2023, but Rowena remained a stockholder while serving as vice president.

The NBI said they are investigating the link between the two resorts as SEC records showed that the same individuals are serving as officers in both, while the incorporators share the same address. Individuals handling corporate filings for one resort also appeared on the records of the other.
Matibag said they will continue to investigate crucial documents to identify how these properties were acquired, who the owners are, and where the funds came from.

articles.title: Germany's ex-spy chief arrested for espionage
articles.summary: August Hanning served as the head of Germany's BND foreign intelligence agency from 1998 to 2005. According to German media, he is being investigated for allegedly passing on state secrets and…

image.caption: August Hanning has reportedly been arrested over alleged spying and acting as a secret service agentImage: Michael Kappeler/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Police have arrested the former head of Germany's BND foreign intelligence agency, August Hanning, on suspicion of espionage, the federal prosecutor's office announced Tuesday.
Hanning served as the agency's chief between 1998 and 2005.

According to a statement from the prosecutor's office, he is facing charges including alleged espionage against the state, disclosure of state secrets, attempted treason, and working as a secret service agent.

The statement added that a former high-ranking employee of the BND had also been arrested on suspicion of providing Hanning with hundreds of classified documents in exchange for money over more than a decade.
What else do we know about the investigation?
Police arrested Hanning early Tuesday at his home in Nordwalde near the western German city of Münster, according to information from WDR, NDR and the Süddeutsche Zeitung.
Hanning's alleged accomplice, who was identified only as Manfred D. in line with Germany's privacy laws, was taken into custody in Bavaria.
Authorities were conducting searches at both suspects' properties, as well as in Berlin, the prosecutor said.
During Hanning's tenure as spy chief, D. reportedly served as his chief of staff. He is facing charges of aiding and abetting attempted treason and espionage against the state.

articles.title: Giant underwater Kelvin wave could 'pack a punch' for B.C. in mid-October
articles.summary: A giant underwater wave of water connected to this year's El Niño weather pattern is making its way up the west coast of the Americas, raising alarm bells amongst scientists worried about how climate…

image.caption: Waves and debris crash into the breakwater in Victoria, B.C. in 2024. This year's El Niño will soon send more waves at B.C.'s coast. (Chad Hipolito/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Science

A giant underwater wave of water connected to this year's El Niño weather pattern is making its way up the west coast of the Americas, raising alarm bells amongst scientists worried about how climate change is magnifying the impacts of the naturally-occurring phenomenon.
El Niño phenomenon could worsen the effects of storm surges and high tides
· CBC News
· Posted: Oct 06, 2026 4:00 AM EDT | Last Updated: 31 minutes ago

A giant underwater wave of water connected to this year's El Niño weather pattern is moving up the west coast of the Americas, raising alarm bells among scientists about how climate change is magnifying the impacts of the naturally occurring phenomenon.
The so-called Kelvin wave is not unexpected. But like El Niño as a whole, it is happening on top of human-caused climate change that has already warmed the oceans and atmosphere.

A smaller wave already reached B.C. earlier this summer, and the next one is expected to arrive within one to two weeks, according to Bill Merryfield, a research scientist at Environment and Climate Change Canada.
"We actually did already see over 30 centimetres in some locations in June. And so the coming wave looks like it'll be a stronger one," Merryfield said.
What causes it?

The Kelvin wave is a naturally occurring weather phenomenon, just like El Niño itself. In normal years, winds blow from east to west along the equator in the Pacific Ocean, generally pushing water from South America toward Asia.
During El Niño years, however, those east-to-west winds weaken or can reverse direction, allowing water to move east instead.

"When these Kelvin waves reach the coast of South America, there's nowhere further east for this pile up of water to go. And so it splits and starts running up and down the coasts of the Americas" and eventually all the way up to Canada, Merryfield said.
Sea-level monitoring data collected at Tofino, on Vancouver Island's Pacific coast, shows the impact of the earlier Kelvin wave in June.
Rather than a giant tsunami-like wave, the Kelvin wave temporarily raises sea levels.

"You can think of it more like a very broad, hundreds of miles wide, but very shallow bulge in the height of the ocean surface, so by maybe a foot or so," University of California climate scientist Daniel Swain told CBS News last month.
What will it do to the West Coast?
Merryfield said the impacts are most pronounced during king tides, particularly high tides that happen when the gravitational pull of the sun and moon combine to produce higher-than-normal tides.

"So if you put that 30 centimetres of sea level rise on top of a king tide, and then maybe you add a winter storm to that, which causes a storm surge, that's when you really start to get into trouble," he said.
"This extra foot or so of sea level rise due to El Niño can pack a punch."
El Niño-fuelled heat could kill half a million people by February: study

Those surges could be intensified by another effect of El Niño, further raising sea levels along the B.C coast. El Niño can strengthen northward winds along the coast, pushing even more water toward shore.

These compounding effects — the Kelvin wave, stronger northward winds and winter storms, on top of climate change already raising sea levels and intensifying extreme weather — could worsen flooding and erosion along the coast. Strong El Niños in the past have caused widespread erosion on California's beaches.
Local authorities there are placing emergency sand on beaches and expect the Kelvin wave to raise water levels six to 12 inches, the Associated Press reports.
The impacts of the Kelvin wave — and El Niño more broadly — could extend far beyond this season, Merryfield warned.

The oceans absorb much of the excess heat trapped by greenhouse gases, moderating global warming as humans continue to burn fossil fuels. During El Niños, however, some of that stored heat is released from the ocean into the atmosphere.
This will likely lead to 2027 becoming the warmest year on record "by quite a significant margin," Merryfield said, echoing similar warnings from other climate research organizations and scientists.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Inayat Singh covers the environment and climate change at CBC News. He is based in Toronto and has previously reported from Winnipeg. Email: inayat.singh@cbc.ca
